title: MuSeToM: Multi-Sensory Evaluation of Belief Revision with Textual Cues Across Six Senses
abstract: arXiv:2611.16662v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Theory of Mind (ToM), the ability to infer mental states in others, is pivotal for human social cognition. Existing evaluations of ToM in large language models (LLMs) mainly focus on static belief attribution and false-belief reasoning, leaving a critical aspect of social reasoning underexplored: can LLMs decide whether perceptual evidence is sufficient to justify another person's belief revision? To address this gap, we present MuSeToM, a human-validated, text-based benchmark for evaluating epistemic belief revision in ToM reasoning. MuSeToM contains 2,415 instances adapted from BigToM and OpenToM, with textual cues spanning six sensory categories, and tests whether models can determine when a protagonist should revise a belief and infer the resulting updated belief state. translated_title: MuSeToM：基于六种感官文本线索的信念修正多感官评估
translated_abstract: 心理理论，即推断他人心理状态的能力，是人类社会认知的关键。现有对大型语言模型心理理论能力的评估主要集中于静态信念归属和错误信念推理，而社会推理中一个关键方面尚未得到充分探索：大型语言模型能否判断感知证据是否足以支持另一个人修正其信念？为填补这一空白，我们提出了MuSeToM——一个经过人类验证的、基于文本的基准，用于评估心理理论推理中的认知性信念修正。MuSeToM包含2,415个改编自BigToM和OpenToM的实例，其文本线索涵盖六种感官类别，测试模型能否判断主人公何时应当修正信念，并推断出更新后的信念状态。利用MuSeToM，我们在直接提示和思维链提示下系统评估了最先进的大型语言模型，揭示出一种显著的不协调现象：尽管模型往往……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了经过人类验证的MuSeToM基准，通过涵盖六种感官类别的文本线索，首次系统评估大型语言模型能否判断感知证据何时足以触发心理理论中的信念修正，并推断出更新后的信念状态。
en_tdlr: MuSeToM, a human-validated benchmark with 2,415 instances spanning six sensory categories of textual cues, systematically evaluates whether LLMs can determine when perceptual evidence justifies belief revision and infer the resulting updated belief states in Theory of Mind reasoning.
